transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Honestly, I feel like the warm part of me has shut off. I sit with my husband or put on shows I normally like after work, and I know I should feel comforted or maybe a little happy, but there’s just... nothing there.
Did this start after a specific stressful event or major life change?
Yeah. It started about three weeks ago, after a pallet collapsed at work and injured my coworker.
Do unwanted memories of the accident keep popping into your mind?
Yeah. It comes out of nowhere—I’ll see the pallet falling again or hear that crash in my head. Especially if a forklift beeps or somebody drops something in the warehouse. My stomach just turns.
Have you been having nightmares about the accident?

Not exactly nightmares, but most nights I can’t get to sleep. I’m exhausted, then as I start drifting off I jerk awake thinking I heard pallets shifting. And when I do sleep, I wake up feeling like I never really rested.
Have you been avoiding reminders of the accident?
I’m not really sure what counts as avoiding reminders. I mean, I still have to be at work, so I can’t completely avoid that area or the equipment.
Since the accident, have you been trying to avoid thoughts or feelings about what happened?
I’m not sure. What do you mean by avoiding the thoughts or feelings?
Since the accident, when thoughts or feelings about it come up, do you try to push them away or not let yourself think about it?
I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed myself doing that on purpose.
Since the accident, have there been moments when it feels like it’s happening again right then, as if you’re back there?
Yeah. Sometimes, out of nowhere, I see that pallet coming down again, like I’m back there. Or if a forklift beeps or somebody drops something, I hear the crash in my head and my stomach just turns.
Has this been going on for longer than one month?
No, it’s been about three weeks—since the pallet collapsed and my coworker got hurt.
Since the accident, have you been staying away from reminders of it whenever you can?
I’m not really sure. What kinds of reminders do you mean?
Since the accident, have you been trying to stay away from things that remind you of it, like that part of the warehouse or the equipment involved?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought about whether I’m avoiding things or not.
Since the accident, have you been feeling constantly on guard or watchful, like something bad might happen again?
Yeah. Near receiving, I’m constantly checking the racks, how high the pallets are, where the exits are, who’s moving behind me. It’s like I can’t trust the floor to be safe for even a minute.
Since the accident, have you been trying to stay away from the part of the warehouse where it happened?
I honestly don’t know. I haven’t paid attention to whether I’m avoiding that area or not.
Since the accident, have you been feeling down or sad most of the day?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed feeling sad most of the day.
Since the accident, have you been trying to stay away from sounds like forklift beeps because they remind you of what happened?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed whether I’m trying to avoid those sounds or not.
Since the accident, have you been going out of your way to avoid the part of the warehouse where it happened?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really noticed myself going out of my way to avoid that area.
Since the accident, have there been important parts of what happened that you still can’t remember?

I remember the stack leaning and people yelling, but right after it fell there’s just a blank spot. I know I must’ve moved or called for help or something, but I can’t piece that part together no matter how hard I try.
Since the accident, when memories of it come up, do you try to push them out of your mind?
I don’t know. I mean, the memories come up, but I haven’t really noticed whether I’m deliberately trying to push them away.
Since the accident, have you been unable to feel positive emotions, like warmth, comfort, or happiness?

Honestly, yeah. I sit with my husband or put on shows I usually like after work, and I know I should feel comforted or a little happy, but... there’s just nothing there. It feels like the warm part of me shut off.
Since the accident, have you been going out of your way to avoid thoughts or reminders of what happened?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself going out of my way to avoid things, exactly.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient developed a trauma-related syndrome within 3 weeks of witnessing a serious workplace accident involving injury to a coworker. She reports intrusive memories/flashback-like re-experiencing, hypervigilance, sleep disturbance, dissociative amnesia for part of the event, and inability to feel positive emotions. Duration is under 1 month, which rules against PTSD at this time. Symptoms are specifically trauma-related rather than a broader maladaptive response to stress, making acute stress reaction/disorder the best fit among the listed options.
